rationale: Frozen objective is latency_ms of one complete batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward on a single GPU, measured as wall time across torch.cuda.synchronize() boundaries (resnet_inference.py:42-47) with GPU-resident input, TF32 and cudnn.benchmark disabled. Trace evidence shows a clean eager forward: coverage.json reports 88 CUDA kernels, all 88 associated below project scope, 0 backward/autograd/ambiguous sequences, and observations.json reports communication not_applicable for the single-device task. Attribution is therefore complete, so the optional nsys run is not selected (no overlap, graph-tracing, or attribution question remains). With no collectives, nccl_tuning and collective_calibration are not applicable, and no PCIe/NVLink traffic may be inferred from payload sizes, leaving no role for device_telemetry: its device-wide NVML samples in native windows cannot be attributed to the millisecond-scale measured invocation, the measured unit contains no host transfer, and kernel-level busy/idle structure is better resolved from timelines. The one unresolved question for latency reduction is how the synchronized wall time splits between host dispatch/launch of the 88 eager kernels and GPU execution: execution_timeline is selected for its separate plain Torch trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization points, and per-device busy/idle intervals to quantify launch-bound gaps inside the measured call (accepting that only CPU-submission clock-alignment bounds are reported), and python_runtime is selected for a warmed cProfile call trace to locate host dispatch and layer-binding hotspots (diagnostic only; it perturbs execution and its times are not clean latency scores or GPU durations). binding_cost and candidate_diagnostics are inapplicable before any candidate exists, and the already-run torch collector is not re-requested.
